newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher on shortcovering.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Wednesday, recovering partially from life-of-contract lows seen in most contracts Tuesday.
"We saw some shortcovering and buying by short term traders looking for a bottom in gold and silver," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
"It was a nice bounce, but largely expected after selling off for a couple of weeks and could be an important reversal day if we see more gains tomorrow," he said.
COMEX February gold ended up $2.10 an ounce at $372.50, recovering from contract lows at $367.70.
Estimated volume in gold futures was 42,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $370.70/371.20, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $370.90, and up from the New York close Tuesday around $368.40/90.
COMEX March silver ended up $1.70 at $4.862 an ounce, after recovering from Tuesday's contract lows at $4.710.
Estimated volume in silver futures was 14,000 lots.
"But the fundamentals haven't changed, so I think the market is still vulnerable unless spot gold gets back above about $375.00," Mitsui USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.

"There's been some nervousness about Tuesday's drop in the Dow Jones index, but it may take a much bigger correction to drive investors back into gold, and with large scale selling of puts options already protecting the downside, we may not see a major equity market correction until next year," he said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 79 points or 1.2 percent Tuesday and was down 37 points near the close Wednesday, but gained 500 points in November to an all time high at 6,606 points.
"In the meantime we've seen some project related hedging by smaller Australian gold miners in the last couple of days, but the majors are well covered," he said.
The price of gold in Australian dollars has recovered to around $464 an ounce from lows around $450 in the past two days, following a fall from around $485 in mid-November.
On Tuesday spot gold in U.S. dollars fell to a new three year low around $366.00, on renewed fears of central bank sales, along with strength in the U.S. dollar against the mark and yen.

Rumors Tuesday of the Bank of Italy selling gold followed news in late November of a proposal to take Switzerland off its quasi-gold standard ahead of the introduction of European monetary union in 1999.
News Wednesday from the U.S. Congressional commission exmaining the U.S. CPI calculation was also bearish long term, analysts said.

The commission, headed by former Bush administration economist, Michael Boskin, said the U.S. CPI overstated inflation by 1.1 percentage points per year and recommended the basis of the CPI index be changed.
With U.S. inflation already below 3.0 pct since 1993, there was little need for gold as an inflation hedge, analysts said.

Gold has been in a long term downtrend from five year highs at $417.70 seen in February 1996, but the downtrend accelerating in the past two weeks, dragging popular technical indicators down to oversold levels, suggesting a short term bounce was now likely, traders said.
NYMEX January platinum closed up $2.20 at $378.20 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium was up $1.70 at $118.75.
Both platinum group metals contracts saw life-of-contract lows Tuesday.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk,+1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
